Start slower than you think you need to. Most beginners go out too fast, get winded in two minutes, and decide running is not for them.

Try a run-walk plan. Run for one minute, walk for two, and repeat for about twenty minutes. Do that three days a week with a rest day between each session. After a couple of weeks, make the running intervals longer and the walking shorter. Within two months, most people can run twenty or thirty minutes without stopping.

A few practical things help. Get a pair of proper running shoes from a store that will watch you jog. Run at a pace where you could still hold a conversation. If something hurts in a sharp way, stop and rest rather than pushing through it. Mild soreness in your legs is normal, but pain in a joint is not.

Do not worry about distance or speed at first. The goal in the early weeks is just to build the habit and let your body adapt.
